topics.label: Lecture introduction: cancer evolution, cell of origin, and the microenvironment
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by outlining the lecture's core themes in cancer evolution alongside the intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cell-intrinsic genetic mutations and epigenetic modifications confer selective advantages that drive clonal expansion and Darwinian selection in tissues.

topics.label: Stemness, tissue hierarchy, and cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how cellular hierarchy, stemness properties, and specific cells of origin govern tumor initiation and propagation across hematological and epithelial tissue models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental regulation, analytical approaches, and evolutionary synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how extrinsic microenvironmental cues and inflammatory interactions drive malignant growth, extending to the spatial methods used to map these interactions and an integrated synthesis of cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next lecture preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with closing remarks and previews the upcoming topic of cancer therapy.
